title: Affine-line evaluation and the composite exceptional transpose
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes and morphisms below are separated finite type over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work with the small pro-etale derived categories, derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and $D^b_{ctf}$ as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$ and $\rho$ for the right tensor unitor. For an affine-line projection $u:L\to B$ [def-sbc-affine-space], set $F_uH=Lu^*H\otimes A_L(1)[2]$ and let $t_B:Ru_!A_L(1)[2]\to A_B$ be the normalized integration of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Let $\Pi^u_H:Ru_!F_uH\xrightarrow{\sim}H\otimes Ru_!A_L(1)[2]$ be exactly its inverse projection transformation with the two tensor symmetries, and put
$$b_{u,H}=\rho_H(1_H\otimes t_B)\Pi^u_H:Ru_!F_uH\longrightarrow H.$$
For $H\in D^b_{ctf}(B,A)$ these maps form a natural transformation, and under the canonical tensor-unit identifications
$$b_{u,A_B}=t_B.$$
Let $p:X\to Y$, let $q:\mathbf A^1_X\to X$, and let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Use the constructible exceptional adjoints and their counits $\varepsilon$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Then $Rp^!K$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, so $\gamma_{q,Rp^!K}$ of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] is defined. For any $\theta:M\to Rp^!K$, set
$$J=\varepsilon_{p,K}Rp_!(\theta):Rp_!M\to K,\qquad
\alpha=\alpha_{p,q}:Rp_!Rq_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(pq)_!,$$
where $\alpha$ is the normalized comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and let $c:R(pq)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq^!Rp^!$ be its adjunction conjugate with the composite adjunction convention [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The actual exceptional transpose of
$$\Theta=c_K^{-1}\gamma_{q,Rp^!K}F_q(\theta):F_qM\longrightarrow R(pq)^!K$$
satisfies
$$\varepsilon_{pq,K}R(pq)_!(\Theta)=J\,Rp_!(b_{q,M})\,\alpha_{F_qM}^{-1}.$$
All source complexes in these adjunctions are bounded below of etale origin; no ambient exceptional adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale complexes is asserted.

proof.text: First check admissibility using the existing ordinary etale preservation API. For the given representative Ke, its bounded-below property makes the unit Ke -> Rnu_* nu^* Ke an isomorphism. Compose that isomorphism with Rnu_*(eK) to identify Ke with Rnu_* K, and transport ordinary constructible finite-Tor membership across it. The coefficient exponent ell^(level+1) annihilates the finite ring and is invertible on the target. Apply AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.constructibleFiniteTor_rightDerivedUpperShriek (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Stability.UpperShriek) to Rnu_* K. By definition its output is exceptionalAntecedent, proving exceptionalInput without chart bounds or reflection of pro-etale finite-Tor membership. The same ordinary preservation argument applies to q and pq. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), $M,K,N,Rq^!N,R(pq)^!K$ have bounded etale representatives; hence the counits $\varepsilon_{q,N}$, $\varepsilon_{p,K}$, $\varepsilon_{pq,K}$, the composite counit and the units used for the conjugate $c$ are all evaluated on bounded-below etale-origin objects. The construction in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] gives bounded-below etale-origin witnesses for $F_qM,F_qN$ (exact pullback followed by tensor with the etale Tate line and shift by $2$). By [thm-sf-comp-composition], $Rq_!$ preserves the bounded-below etale-origin class, so $Rq_!F_qM$ is also an allowed source for the $p$-adjunction. The natural Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2)--(3), as used in that definition, therefore apply to all the displayed objects and respect the chosen comparisons. No adjunction on other pro-etale source objects is needed.

source.place: Integration paragraph, affine-line counit and inductive formula Tr_{p_j}=Tr_{p_{j-1}} composed with Rp_{j-1!}(Tr_{r_j}); expanded by an agent into the normalized exceptional-transpose identity

proof.text:
Put $T=A_L(1)[2]$ and $V=Ru_!T$. The canonical projection map is natural in its second input and invertible on these inputs by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; with the two symmetries specified in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], its inverse gives, for $h:H\to H'$,
$$\Pi^u_{H'}\,Ru_!(F_uh)=(h\otimes1_V)\Pi^u_H.$$
The trace $t_B:V\to A_B$ is fixed. Tensor bifunctoriality and naturality of the right unitor now give
$$b_{u,H'}Ru_!(F_uh)=\rho_{H'}(1\otimes t_B)(h\otimes1_V)\Pi^u_H=h\rho_H(1\otimes t_B)\Pi^u_H=h b_{u,H}.$$
This is the required natural transformation; it also applies to $h=\theta:M\to N$.

source.place: Integration paragraph, affine-line counit and inductive formula Tr_{p_j}=Tr_{p_{j-1}} composed with Rp_{j-1!}(Tr_{r_j}); expanded by an agent into the normalized exceptional-transpose identity

proof.text:
Check the tensor-unit component of the actual projection map, rather than merely its invertibility. At the chosen compactification $(j,r)$ of $u$, [def-exchange-projection] defines $\operatorname{PF}_{u,T,A_B}$ as the proper projection map followed by $Rr_*$ of the open tensor comparison. The proper map is the identity under the tensor-unit identifications by the last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The open comparison is also the identity under these identifications: [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] makes its restriction the identity and makes derived $j_!$ fully faithful, hence restriction detects equality between these two maps of objects in its image. Thus $\operatorname{PF}_{u,T,A_B}$ is the identity after the canonical unit identifications. The inner symmetry $A_L\otimes T\to T\otimes A_L$ becomes the identity and the outer symmetry $V\otimes A_B\to A_B\otimes V$ becomes $\lambda_V^{-1}$, with $\lambda$ the left unitor. Hence $\Pi^u_{A_B}=\lambda_V^{-1}$, and
$$b_{u,A_B}=\rho_{A_B}(1\otimes t_B)\lambda_V^{-1}=t_B,$$
by naturality of $\lambda$ and $\rho_{A_B}=\lambda_{A_B}$.

proof.text:
For $N=Rp^!K$ the definition of the line comparison is exactly $\gamma_{q,N}=\Phi_q(b_{q,N})$ [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Inverting its adjunction Hom bijection gives
$$\varepsilon_{q,N}\,Rq_!(\gamma_{q,N})=b_{q,N}.$$
Precompose with $Rq_!F_q(\theta)$ and use Step 2 to obtain the equality of maps $Rq_!F_qM\to N$
$$\varepsilon_{q,N}\,Rq_!(\gamma_{q,N}F_q\theta)=b_{q,N}Rq_!F_q\theta=\theta b_{q,M}.$$
This uses only the defining transpose, not isomorphy of the purity comparison.

source.place: Integration paragraph, affine-line counit and inductive formula Tr_{p_j}=Tr_{p_{j-1}} composed with Rp_{j-1!}(Tr_{r_j}); expanded by an agent into the normalized exceptional-transpose identity

proof.text:
Write $P=Rp_!$, $Q=Rq_!$, $V=R(pq)_!$, and $R=R(pq)^!$. The counit of $PQ\dashv Rq^!Rp^!$ is
$$e_K=\varepsilon_{p,K}\,P(\varepsilon_{q,Rp^!K})$$
by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. By the conjugate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and the equivalent transpose formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the conjugate $c$ of $\alpha:PQ\to V$ satisfies
$$e_K\,PQ(c_K)=\varepsilon_{pq,K}\,\alpha_{RK}.$$
For any arrow $a:W\to RK$, naturality of $\alpha$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{pq,K}V(a)\alpha_W=e_K\,PQ(c_Ka).$$
These equations concern the normalized $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and exactly its conjugate, so there is no additional choice of a right-adjoint isomorphism. Since $\alpha_W$ is invertible, this calculates the actual $pq$-transpose as $e_KPQ(c_Ka)\alpha_W^{-1}$.

source.place: Integration paragraph, affine-line counit and inductive formula Tr_{p_j}=Tr_{p_{j-1}} composed with Rp_{j-1!}(Tr_{r_j}); expanded by an agent into the normalized exceptional-transpose identity

proof.text:
Apply Step 5 with $W=F_qM$ and $a=\Theta=c_K^{-1}\gamma_{q,N}F_q\theta$. Cancel $c_Kc_K^{-1}$ and use the equality in Step 4 inside $P$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{pq,K}R(pq)_!(\Theta)
&=\varepsilon_{p,K}\,P\bigl(\varepsilon_{q,N}Q(\gamma_{q,N}F_q\theta)\bigr)\alpha_{F_qM}^{-1}\\
&=\varepsilon_{p,K}\,P(\theta b_{q,M})\alpha_{F_qM}^{-1}\\
&=(\varepsilon_{p,K}P\theta)\,P(b_{q,M})\alpha_{F_qM}^{-1}\\
&=J\,Rp_!(b_{q,M})\alpha_{F_qM}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is functoriality of $P$, and the last line is the definition of $J$. This proves the stated identity for every $\theta$.
